# Branch: c/exciting-tesla-z07s4b

Implements **UP-008**: `up` must refuse to deploy a bundle onto host state
that belongs to a different bundle, naming what it found there and changing
nothing, and must stay safe to repeat against state belonging to the same
bundle (UP-003).

Today every deployment lays its state out the same way under
`<RemoteDir>/state`, and nothing on the host says whose state that is. A
second bundle deployed to a directory a first one is already using takes it
over: Forgejo boots against a database written by another instance, whose
`SECRET_KEY` no longer matches it, so sessions, CSRF tokens, and every
secret that database holds become undecryptable — and nothing fails at
deploy time to say so.

Work:

1. **Record whose state this is**, on the host beside `forgejo-version` and
   `compose-project` — the records that already describe a deployment rather
   than the forge. The identity is the instance's SSH host key fingerprint:
   it is bundle identity (spec.md "Identity" > "Key material"), it never
   rotates, it survives `attach` filling in a domain (UP-007), and a nameless
   bundle has one too. The bundle domain rides along as a human label so the
   refusal can name the instance rather than only a fingerprint.
2. **Refuse in `deploy.Up`**, before anything on the host is touched, when
   that record names a different instance — naming what it found and what
   this bundle is, and saying what to do instead.
3. **Cover instances deployed before the record existed.** A host with no
   record falls back to the SSH host key `up` itself installed under
   `state/gitea`, so a live instance is protected on the very first `up` of
   a binary carrying this change rather than only after one re-deploy.
4. **`restore` stamps the record** for the state it places, beside the
   `forgejo-version` stamp it already writes, so recovery onto a reused host
   keeps working.

Nothing about snapshot verification, the four-kind state model, or the
identity model changes.

See `docs/functional-requirements.md` § UP and `docs/status.json`.

This file exists for conductor tracking and can be deleted once the PR
merges.
